The animals are corralled to be fed and kept in a certain (quite large) area of the river to be washed, but otherwise roam around a large natural reserve. 

Some of the extras put on for tourists (photos with the elephants, feeding/washing them etc) arent acceptable. The elephants are wild animals, not playthings or props, and they should be treated as such. A couple of keepers rode some of the bulls back from the river, which again I dont agree with. Additionally, perhaps more effort could be made to return some of the animals back to the wild, however I dont know anything about the practicalities  and of course this runs the risk of them being killed by farmers (the main threat to wild elephants in Sri Lanka).

All in all, as far as I could tell the Pinnewala Orphanage is not abusive to the animals in its care and is no worse than Western zoos. Keeping animals in captivity is never ideal, but the fraught relationship between farmers and wildlife in Sri Lanka make it impossible for all elephants to live in the wild. Perhaps in the future with better education, people all over the world will be better able to co-exist with animals and places like Pinnewala will be unnecessary. However, for now this place is the best of a bad situation.

title: Place To Avoid
content: This sea turtle hatchery centre is a worrying concept. While I accept that there will always be those turtles that require help and assistance due to injury or birth defects, this place appears to be more of a sordid tourist attraction whose primary aim is to make money.  The entrance fee is 2000 Sri Lankan rupees,  and upon entry, the poor turtles are kept in small, unclean tanks, swimming aimlessly around in circles.  Yes, they are cute and are such beautiful animals,  but I do not believe that they are truly cared for or treated with love and affection. I believe that this was once a genuine going concern,  but now has simply become a way to make human' s money at the expense of these serene animals.  AVOID AT ALL COSTS, if you genuinely care for wildlife. This is simply a zoo. DISGUSTING!
location_name: Sea Turtle Farm Galle Mahamodara, Galle

title: Feels dodgy
content:
When this was advertised as a conservation effort I was excited. I have had some great experiences with turtles in the wild. They are amazing, intelligent, beautiful animals. I paid the 500 rupee entrance fee and was immediately disappointed after walking in. They had large turtles alone in very small tanks (about the size of a single bed), these poor creatures were lifted out of the tank and passed around for each tour group that went through (about 5-10 mins apart).  A couple were obviously injured and I do believe that they wouldn't have survived in the wild, but I'm not convinced that their current circumstances are necessarily preferable. One (which didn't have any obvious injury) was showing signs of distress and biting the edge of the concrete tank. There were chunks missing from a few places of the tank, so she'd obviously been at it for a while despite the fact that we were told she was only there temporarily.

The baby turtles were listless, but I don't think I saw any dead ones. They have a hatchery at the back of the compound which is ostensibly the main part of the conservation effort. They pay locals to bring them eggs from the beach so that they can incubate and hatch away from predators (dogs and birds). I'm sure it has nothing to do with the 1000 rupees they can charge tourists to release a baby into the wild. 

The guide was knowledgeable and friendly enough. When asked whether the centre was involved in any conservation research or formal programs the answer was no.

Overall I was extremely disappointed and feel very guilty for giving my money to this business. I thought long and hard about writing this review because it may be that there is a genuine desire to perform some conservation efforts, however the more i think about it the more sinister it seems.

If you are genuinely interested in turtles, I'd advise you to take your chances and go on one of the may dive/snorkelling tours that are available in southern Sri Lanka. If you just want to see a turtle and have no concern for it's welfare, then this will fulfil your needs
location_name: Sea Turtle Farm Galle Mahamodara, Galle

title: Uninspiring nature walk
content:
We were not overly impressed having already been to places like Sinharaja rainforest for a hike and Udawawale national park for safari. 

Its close to Kandy central and we stopped off during a day exploring on tuk tuk. 

The forest loop walk took us just over an hour. Whether or not this was due to timing/time of year we will never know but we really didnt see much wildlife. We visited around 3pm so perhaps why. We heard some birds and perhaps some monkeys but saw none on our walk. 

The trees etc are beautiful as always in Sri Lanka but we didnt feel that with the walk was warranting of the foreigner price of 1750 rupees for me and my wife included.

Also beware of many leeches on the walk. Would avoid wearing sandals like we did - silly from our side. 

Its nice enough but there are better walks in nature in Sri Lanka which are better maintained.

title: Amazing jungle; just mind the scamming Rangers
content:
This park is just incredible. The rangers at the front who sell tickets are scammers through. The entrance fee is 650 rupees. So I counted out 6 x 100 rupee notes and one 50 rupee note. They said ok and gave me a map (no ticket) but just 30 seconds after walking off they called me back and said that I was short 100 rupees. While my back was turned they pocketed one of the 100 rupee notes leaving only 5 on the counter. It was pointless to argue so I just handed over one more. 

Despite this the sanctuary is beautiful and well worth a visit. It's 250 acres just behind the Temple of the Tooth. Head west from the Temple up the street with the Pizza Hut and the Queen hotel on the corner. Go about 400m and turn right at the first set of traffic lights. Follow the winding road up the hill (easily walkable). 

The rainforest is pristine as it has been preserved by the Kings since the 1200s. The walking trails are well marked and easy. There are troops of monkeys which show no interest in people and which, unlike elsewhere in SE Asia are not aggressive and just walk calmly past you as if you're not there.  It's amazing to walk past a whole family of monkeys so close (within a metre) while they mind their own business, carrying their babies and grooming each other with none of the aggressive behaviour you usually see in monkeys that live this close to humans. In a 2 hour visit I also saw wild boar and tiny deer. It's so peaceful and lovely and incredible to think it's an easy 20 min walk from Kandy city. Just closely watch what you pay as you go in!

title: A truly wild park - not Longleat
content:
We did 2 safaris at Wilpattu. One was an afternoon safari and one was an all day safari. 
Wilpattu is a big park and there are less roads than at Yala, but there are also a lot less jeeps, and for much of our wildlife viewing we were on our own. During our afternoon safari we watched a sloth bear feeding from a termite nest very close to the road. We were able to sit there for around 20 minutes and during that time we were joined by maybe half a dozen other jeeps - a complete contrast to Yala where around 30 jeeps were competing for a view of a sloth bear which was much further away from the road.
We saw lots of animals and birds. We didn't see a leopard but we saw plenty of evidence that they were around - lots of very recent footprints in the sand - it's down to luck whether you actually see one or not, but the chance is obviously increased by the number of safaris you undertake.
There is a place where they stop for lunch and breakfast where there is also a basic hole in the ground type toilet. Beware of all the monkeys there, who will steal your food at any opportunity!
As expected it is a very bumpy ride in the jeep and my husband suffered a bit as he has some joint problems - especially during the all day safari, which lasted from 6.15am to 6.00pm. However the advantage of the all day safari is that they can take you much further into the park, away from any other jeeps. This park is not for kids who will easily get bored - but it is a genuinely immersive wildlife experience.

title: Worth a stop if you're passing by
content: This place is certainly worth a stop if you're passing by, but I definitely wouldn't pay a tuk tuk to take me there. Yes it's impressive, yes it's beautiful, but it was packed with people, and there's really no place to just sit and soak in the feel of the place. Five or ten minutes, a few photos, and you're on your way. On the plus side, it's free. Also, I rode there from Ella on a scooter, and the ride itself was beautiful, enjoyable ride even without a waterfall. Beware of the beggers and of the snack sellers. I was charged an absolutely extortionist price on a coconut and some roti. One last note - some people hike in to the top of the falls. Perhaps this would've been a better experience?

title: Awful, inhumane and filthy environment for Animals!!!!
content: Filthy awful zoo, my heart broke for the animals living in those conditions. We where charged $70 AUD for a family (4 times higher than the locals one thing I don't think encourages tourists to visit and let me tell you it was NOT worth it because I don't think much of that money goes to the poor creatures). The facilities where in a disgraceful state of neglect, we saw rotten food in the animal feed trays, rubbish everywhere. The entrance staff where very rude (because being rude to tourists really lures them in...crazy)! The toilet facilities OMG don't even ask about the state of those....disgusting!!!!! We left  feeling angry and really upset about the welfare of the animals! Apparently they get the elephants to perform, but all we saw was them chained up with a chain around each leg. But it was the state in which they where kept  :( It was the lowest point for our trip to Sri Lanka!!! Something needs to be done about that zoo!!!
location_name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka, Colombo

title: Inhumane and cruel
content:
I will just start with a straight "avoid". I was taken here by a Sri Lankan family friend, who told us we were going out for the day in Colombo. I don't mean to be so harsh on somewhere but it's not hard to see when animals are suffering. If you care about the welfare of animals at all, you really shouldn't go, as animals are kept in small cages, look very distressed and unhealthy. Let this be an indicator: they still hold elephant shows, where elephants lift their legs not because they have been 'trained' to do so, but because they have been repeatedly prodded in the leg with a sharp rod and are now avoiding it.
I'm very 'for' the growth of Sri Lanka's economy and tourism industry, but please do not visit this zoo.
location_name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka, Colombo

title: An average National Zoo but the ticket price is quite steep even for a foreigner...
content:
Ayubowan! 

Visited this place on 21st December 2014 with a local buddy.

The location is easily reached by public buses. Upon reaching the Zoo entrance, I have sensed that something is not quite right as street peddlers, beggars are all over the place and the entrance is quite dirty littered with garbage.

While at the ticket booth, I saw a notice sign telling the entrance fees...Foreigner 2500lkr and Local 100lkr. My friend was surprised with the fees hike since his last visit which was 1500lkr and asked me if I would like to proceed. Since we were already there, why not to go ahead with the plan for the day (we reached about 1.30pm as the weather is drizzling slightly and cool). I really wanted to see and explore a Zoo that is charging high fees as I made Zoo visits a must when visiting foreign countries. 

Well, the first impression at the entrance is already at the point of shocked and disbelieved therefore I do not have high expectation and will now on only highlight the stronger points, enjoy and make the best out of it. First greeting is from the Flamingo on the left and bald bodied Ostrich on the left. Errr...did I mentioned bald bodied ostrich, yup something is wrong. Most of the avian settings are all wet from the weather. The ostriches are losing their feathers and they even have bloodied ends.

Then next salt water aquarium and the fresh water aquarium display. That 'cave tunnel' is very dark with poor or almost no lighting...all you can hear is water dripping in the river setting on the right and the poor tank display on the left...people are pushing their way trough and children are everywhere running...have to be very careful or else you might trip and fall into the 'river'...the 2nd part of the 'cave tunnel' is much better...more lighting and the tank display are more newer and minus the river, more attractive and better maintained. Then at the exit there is a pond with glass viewing panel with hundreds of colorful carps swimming in it. 
In order to cover the compound to the maximum, all you need to do is to follow the cage number direction arrows (1 - 60). The macaw enclosure with yellow dusty soil cover at the bottom are literally infested with rats! They burrowed underneath the ground and feeds on the leftover food from the macaws...then the other cages of the eagle owl and so forth are not spared from litters, dirty water buckets, dried water dish and rusty cage wired mesh walls. What they did was patching up the cage with another layer of mesh. The display cages are basically their permanent home and some has no roosting box eg the african grey parrot. The only lemur collections that can be seen is the lonely ring tailed lemur which loves some head and snout rub...the others maybe inactive. 

Butterfly enclosure is empty too...expected to see all the sri lankan endemic species but...again the enclosure was infested with rats. The waterfall next to the meerkats and ferrets were supposed to house the mute swans but only the domestic goose was seen. We paused the visit at cage no13 because we wanted to see the sealion performance at 4.30pm therefore we adjourn to the sealion arena. It was an open seating place underneath a huge tree but the seating area is soaking wet from the rain and have birds dropping everywhere. The water in the pond where the sealion swims is green and full of leaves litters too. It was a 20 minutes show. 
After the show, we continue from where we stop. 

The open aviary is not really 'open' as peacock, hornbills and white koel are in cages within the aviary. Only ring necks, some fowls and mynah are free flying. Most of the big cats pens are closed for reconstruction, the jungle cats enclosure are dark and smelly...while other bigger animals such as the elephants, tigers, deers, orang utan, rhino and giraffes have fairly bigger enclosure as to compare with the others. Some of the monkeys need medical attention, esp the obese white toque monkey, the formosan monkey that has facial skin problem and they seems lethargy too. Well with the costly entrance fee, the toilets are being charged at 30rs per person. 

As a conclusion, I am 80% happy with this visit as they have quite varied species collected for display. The balance is sad with the avian settings, animal health conditions, the cleanliness and not enough time. Whether if it worth the money paid is up to individuals but indeed this is a pricey one.
location_name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka, Colombo

title: A diverse range of animals to see
content:
Yes, quite a few cages are too small and need renovating, but it is evident to see that slowly the zoo is tackling these issues with a large elephant enclosure renovation going on. I arrived around 10.30am on a Saturday morning nad the keepers had already fed most animals a tasty array of fruits/grass/vege etc and cages were clean or in the process of being cleaned.The animals are not neglected although their housing conditions could be improved. however it was interesting to see such a wide range of animals, and the zoo was quite well laid out. People watching is almost as much fun as the animals, and there are so many cute little Sri Lankan kids around. I didn't try to restuarnats but icecreams and drinks were widely avaialble in the park. Entry a little expensive for foreigners but all information panels have at least one section for english. I went by myself, and as a single lady traveller, was pleased not to be hasseled or nagged by anyone during my visit. Beware of the touts outside peddling fruit and plastic kitsch. Happily I had a driver waiting for me, but unless you are confident with the bus system, I would recommend taking a tuk-tuk or a taxi to the zoo. It would take quite a long time by bus from Colombo.

Your ticket includes the priveledge of the tourist loos (chargeable one) but mae sure to take your own loo paper. A great way to spend a few hours, and probably best to visit in the morning when the zoo first opens to avoid the crowds.
location_name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka, Colombo

title: AN ABSOLUTE SHOCKER!!!
content: i've visited many zoo's before around the world but this one has to top them all of being the WORST zoo i have ever been to in my life! i was sicken and distaught and absolutely disgusted at the way the animals were kept in this place. i've added some pics please check to see how the animals are being kept. The most shocking for me was these fish called arapaima which are very large fish and the tank that they were in was not enough even for them to move around in. I felt sick! the second reason and final which made me just walk out of the place was the elephants and how they were tied up to the chains. i understand to tame and control these elephant a chain is often placed around the neck and around the ankle so they don't start running off but despite that i prefer that were at least the animal can still move around freely but at the zoo they were all 15 of them were tied up with the back leg and the front so much so that they had no movement what so ever to move around. what broke me down and even now as i'm back home is bringing a tear to my eye was seeing one of the elephant looking at me and it raised one of its chained legs. now you don't have to be a zoologist to realise that it was saying to me please release this off my leg. absolute heart breaking!!. These guys that should be looking at the walfare of these animals have absolutely no regard for them what so ever. i don't know. maybe in this part of the world its acceptable to treat animals like this but any person who has a humain side to them would thick once before doing what the zoo keepers are doing in colombo zoo. i would recommend foreigners stay away from this hell hole that charges 2,000 rupees to see what hell animals are living in!!
location_name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka, Colombo

title: Rip off - 20 times higher entry fee for foreigners.....
content: The first thing what I noticed was that Sri Lankan nationals have to pay 100 Rp but everyone else 2,000. This is a rip off. The zoo itself has nice gardens but the cages for the animals are old, too small and dirty. You really feel for them in their much too small prison. Can't recommend it at all.
location_name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka, Colombo

title: A Zoo Which Requires A Lot Of Improvement
content:
If you are a tourist looking for things to do during your stay in Colombo-avoid the zoo. You d be disappointed at the price you pay to enter, the conditions of facilities, health of animals. 

Dehiwela Zoo used to be much better managed not too long ago. Its spread over a large area with amazing scenery and wide ranging terrain. It also had a large collection of animals. But somethings gone wrong somewhere down the line and the zoo requires serious attention of relevant authority.
location_name: National Zoological Gardens of Sri Lanka, Colombo

title: Worst experience. Asking for entry fees in a Buddhist temple. SHAMEFUL!!!
content: Shameful experience!!! Asking for entry fees n buddhist temple is like selling the religion for petty gains.i was refused entry as I was not willing to pay then it came to donation. I'm a proud hindu from India and this I have not seen in any part of the world I have visited. Buddhism is one of the most spiritual religion I feel away from all materialistic charms. But people at this temple are robbing the visitors asking for entry fee and refusing people who are not willing to pay. I even complained to a cop there but seems he was a part of the charity show. I told some foreigners entry is free and people started fighting with me why are you telling to others. After a long argument I finally went in but had lost the spirit by then so could not concentrate. Thereafter not visited any temple in colombo.

title: Constantly bugged for extra cash. Somewhat overhyped.
content:
It was okay. We both felt we had seen better temples. The staff we quite rude and abrupt. We were hounded by people to be our guides as we approached the temple. To the point where we had to shout no and they wouldnt take no for an answer. As foreigners we had to pay 3000 which was a lot we felt. A so called guide even followed us into the check in gate and got annoyed when we politely said no thank you. More persistence. Then we were told without a guide we wouldnt understand. This is not true as just about everything is translated to English. There was a booth to leave our shoes at and when we returned we were hounded again for money for looking after our shoes. We already paid far more than we expected to get in so no thanks! A staff member followed us around when we were in a museum and made me show my ticket a number of times. It all felt like harassment. We are really not made of money, quite the opposite in fact. Something I thought was strange is even though you have to remove your shoes, all the staff didnt which made me ponder what was the point. How can it be rude for us to wear shoes and not them? The tooth display itself was okay but of course you could
Not see it so who is to say it was really there?

Hey we can appreciate the religious/cultural significance - we arent made of stone but we had heard Sri Lankan people were welcoming: They are when they want your cash!
location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic, Kandy

title: Religious significance
content: This temple is the main attraction in kandy for locals and tourists. However, they rip off the tourists with high entrance fees while the locals go in for free.  This temple is meant to house the tooth of lord buddha but visitors cannot actually see it. It's nice inside but very busy.  Dress standards are strict to enter the temple. Ladies need to wear clothing which extends below knee level and also covers shoulders.  Men need to wear long pants and shirts. There are a lot of guides at the entrance who will take you in to explain things and charge around 1000 rupees. Try and get a good guide fluent in english. Also watch out for your valuables as it's very crowded inside.
location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic, Kandy

title: Foreigners Pay High Entrance Fee and locals are free
content:
What is the sense in charging anyone to enter a site that is designated as a place of worship?  Another place where Sri Lankans grab money from foreigners.  

They should stop using animals for their parades held in August.  The elephants are chained and harassed by the mahouts.
location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic, Kandy

title: Not a great experience
content: Not a great experience. Got scammed on storing our shoes (when we wanted to take them in our bag). Ive heard others were scammed by the ticket guides (2,000 LKR is the new price) and those getting guides or taking flowers from people inside also. It was too rammed with no crowd control. An elderly Sri Lankan man fainted it was so packed. Left a bad taste in our mouths for what is supposed to be a deeply religious spot for Buddhists. Also made me dislike Kandy (as scammers had tried us for Tuk Tuks, hotel staff seeing you on the street and taking you to a market, etc. Inside is okay, but hard to know what is what and youre asked for constant donations. Dont bother.
location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic, Kandy

They ushered us into an underground mini theater like we were about to watch a blockbuster Rajinikanth premiere. They've got stones in every color of the rainbow and jewelry that could blind a pirate. Now I'm not a gem guy and my idea of precious stones is a well-shaped barbell, but my friend he fell for the sparkle. He made a purchase fit like a king and then well, let's just say we later found out tourist prices are very real, very expensive thing. Pallet zero, Sri Lanka one. We hit a scenic route and stopped for lunch at a restaurant perched right nearby a waterfall as well as a river and some wonderful scenic hills. The ambience was cool. title: Police warn of Scam Gangs impersonating Senior Officers in Colombo
content: The Police have issued a public warning regarding fraudulent activities carried out by organized groups impersonating senior police officers. According to reports, these groups have been making phone calls to tourist hotels and other private institutions in Colombo, posing as high-ranking police officials. They have allegedly deceived establishments by claiming that food supplies and money were required for various events. Investigations into these scams have already commenced. Police emphasized that such fraudulent activities are being conducted by individuals or organized groups and urged the public and institutions not to be misled. Authorities further requested that anyone with information related to these incidents immediately inform the nearest police station or contact the designated telephone numbers provided.(Newswire)

title: 02 three-wheeler drivers arrested for defrauding tourists
content: Two three-wheeler drivers have been arrested for defrauding two foreign tourists by charging excessive amounts for their travel during their holiday in Sri Lanka. According to the Police, two complaints have been filed with the Tourism Police, after which investigations were launched. The Police said a Brazilian tourist and a Belgian tourist had been charged Rs. 10,000 and Rs. 30,000 during their travels on 02nd and 05th October. The arrested three-wheeler drivers are aged 40 and 48 years, and are residents of Imbulgoda and Wellampitiya. The three-wheeler drivers have been handed over to the Cinnamon Gardens and Colpetty Police Stations for further investigations.(Newswire/ Image- file pic)

title: Upcoming Tourist Season: Statement from Sri Lanka Tourism
content: Sri Lanka Tourism has assured that the highest levels of safety and security will be maintained for all visitors throughout their stay in Sri Lanka. Issuing a statement, Sri Lanka Tourism extended a warm invitation to travellers from around the world to visit the country during the upcoming tourist season. “We ensure that all tourists can enjoy a safe and secure experience while exploring the beauty of our island. The highest levels of safety and security will be maintained for all visitors throughout their stay in Sri Lanka,” it said. Sri Lanka Tourism further said that the Ministry of Defense has also assured that necessary measures have been taken to guarantee the safety of tourists across all areas of the country, ensuring peace of mind for those currently staying in Sri Lanka and for those planning their visits. The assurance comes in the backdrop of several countries issuing travel advisories to Sri Lanka, citing terrorism threats. The US Embassy had initially issued the travel advisory to its citizens, stating that it had received credible information warning of an attack targeting popular tourist locations in the Arugam Bay area. Issuing a clarification on the travel advisory, Police Spokesman Nihal Thalduwa said that the surge in Israeli tourists and the occupation of a building in the Arugam Bay area has prompted the US Embassy in Colombo to issue an advisory. DIG Thalduwa has confirmed that special security measures are currently in place in Arugam Bay, with the involvement of the Police, Special Task Force (STF), Navy, Army, and State Intelligence Services (SIS).(Newswire)

title: Notice for all Israeli nationals in Sri Lanka
content: Sri Lanka Police has introduced a special hotline for Israelis in distress or those needing to ensure their personal safety. “If an Israelite, who has visited Sri Lanka as a tourist or for other purposes, feels the need to ensure his/her personal security, he/she may directly contact the telephone number and get the necessary assistance,” a Police Media Unit statement said. Israeli nationals currently in Sri Lanka are requested to contact the DIG Tourist Range of the Sri Lanka Police via the hotline071-8592651in case they need any assistance or information. The new hotline has been introduced amid warnings of a potential attack on Israelis in the Arugam Bay area. The warning has prompted law enforcement authorities to tighten security in Arugam Bay, while several countries have issued travel warnings to their citizens.(Newswire)
